prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit Image1, our own unapproved raw drawing, with ONE small correction only. Image2 is a diagnostic close-up of the ORIGINAL on the LEFT and our draft on the RIGHT. Image3 is the full original, the sole design/shape authority. Image4 is only the approved flat-color cartoon finish.

Correct ONLY the silhouette of the LARGEST gray piece above the roof, the middle of the three top shapes. The draft makes this gray piece a tilted mathematically regular oval. The source shape in the LEFT close-up has a flattened short top, a flatter more upright right edge with its short projecting end, and an asymmetric broad rounded lower-left face. Follow that precise smooth underlying source contour. Make its left edge slightly less bulging into the empty area, while restoring the source right-hand projection and top/end width. Keep the SAME size, anchor, slant and original muted charcoal/slate face colors. Do not turn the original pixel steps into squared tiles; draw the corresponding smooth irregular metal outline. The small light edge pixels describe a restrained thin source highlight, not a new large shining ring.

Keep EVERYTHING ELSE in Image1 fixed: the two other gray top shapes, every roof contour and shade plane, every wooden post, the body, the lower tiny detached brown pieces, isolated fleck, alpha holes and lower edge. Do not touch any unrelated contour or redraw the whole cabin. Do not add, remove, join or complete any source part. Preserve Image1's exact full-canvas framing and relative drawing size. Keep genuine transparent alpha everywhere already transparent, including the windows and broken lower section, and keep the ceiling opaque. Use solid source colors with restrained anti-aliasing, no texture, gradients, bevels, new black outlines, new seams or details. Output the full single corrected sprite in the same framing as Image1, not an enlargement of the corrected gray part. No labels, dots, comparison, text, guide marks, backdrop, checkerboard, shadow or watermark.
